confirmed.title: Autosave overwrites the unsaved local copy on offer as soon as the user edits before answering the banner
confirmed.failureScenario: Yesterday a conflict or a closed tab left long unsaved text X in localStorage. Today the editor opens the document, and the banner «يوجد تعديل غير محفوظ محليًا» offers X. They ignore it and type one character in any field. One second later the effect writes the current form over the same key, replacing X. If they then leave or reload, X is gone for good. The comment above promises «A copy still on offer stays until the user answers it», and WORK-PACKAGES P04 says a conflict or a closed tab never loses text.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In the autosave effect in CollectionForm.tsx, do not write while an offer is pending: add `if (localOffer) return` before scheduling the setTimeout. Autosave resumes once acceptLocalOffer or discardLocalOffer clears it. The alternative is to hide the fields until the banner is answered.
fixCorrections: Correct and minimal: in the autosave effect, add `if (localOffer) return` right after the equalData block (after line 171, before the setTimeout). The pending timer is already cleared at line 167. After acceptLocalOffer or discardLocalOffer sets `localOffer` to null, the effect runs again (localOffer is in its deps) and autosave resumes.

Put `if (localOffer) return` right after the clearTimeout on line 167, which covers both branches, and drop the now-redundant `!localOffer` check on line 169. Autosave starts again once acceptLocalOffer or discardLocalOffer clears the offer, because `localOffer` is already a dependency of the effect.

Put `if (localOffer) return` right after the clearTimeout at line 167, before the equalData branch. That one guard covers both the write and the removal path, and autosave resumes when acceptLocalOffer or discardLocalOffer sets localOffer to null (it is already a dependency). Edits made while the offer is pending are then not autosaved until the user answers; that is acceptable.
reasons: CONFIRM: While `localOffer` holds X, any edit makes `data` differ from `initialData` (CollectionForm.tsx:168), so the effect skips the removal branch and after 1s writes the current form over the same `draftKey` (lines 172-174). X then survives only in React state. After a reload, readStoredDraft (line 142) returns the new copy, so X is gone. This breaks the promise in the comment at line 164, and PLANS/ISSUES.md does not record it.

CONFIRM: While `localOffer` is set, the banner (CollectionForm.tsx:229) and the editable fields (241-252) both render, and the autosave effect (165-179) only checks `localOffer` in the equal-data branch (169). Any edit makes `data != initialData`, so line 174 writes the current form over the stored draft X one second later. After that, a reload offers only the new edit, and X is gone. This breaks the effect comment at 163-164 and the promise in WORK-PACKAGES P04 that a closed tab never loses text. No guard elsewhere prevents it. It needs the editor to type while ignoring the banner and only affects an unsaved draft on an admin-only page, so I rate it medium, not high.

CONFIRM: CollectionForm.tsx:143 sets localOffer from the stored draft but leaves data equal to initialData; the first keystroke makes equalData false (line 168), so lines 172-175 write the current form over the same draftKey after 1s, and a reload then offers the new edit, not the original copy X. This contradicts the comment at lines 163-164 and the P04 promise in PLANS/WORK-PACKAGES.md:57 («a conflict or a closed tab never loses text»); no ISSUES.md, DECISIONS or DESIGN-AUDIT record covers it. The fix is correct and minimal.

confirmed.title: `storage cp --linked` runs with cwd set to the OS temp dir, outside the linked project, so the default `pnpm backup` cannot resolve the linked project ref
confirmed.evidence: const result = supabase(['storage', 'cp', '-r', `ss:///${bucket}`, `storage/${bucket}`, mode, '--experimental'], { cwd: work })
confirmed.failureScenario: The Supabase CLI finds the project by walking up from its cwd to a `supabase/config.toml`, and reads the link from `<project>/supabase/.temp/project-ref`. The repo's supabase/.temp holds only `cli-latest` today; `supabase link` writes project-ref there. For the download, the script starts the CLI in %TEMP%\anasaq-backup-*, which has no config.toml above it, so `--linked` cannot see the owner's link. The `storage ls` call just before it (cwd = repoRoot) works; the `cp` does not. On the first real `pnpm backup` (default --linked) with any media in media-private, the cp fails with the CLI's not-linked error, or on a TTY asks the owner to pick a project. The script then prints «Downloading bucket media-private failed. No backup was written.», so the owner's only backup path fails whenever a bucket has objects. `--local` works only because the dev stack uses the CLI's default port and JWT secret. The P06 evidence records 'Not run: a --linked backup' (artifacts/acceptance/P06/commands.txt:879), so this path was never exercised.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In scripts/backup.mjs, for mode '--linked', read `join(repoRoot, 'supabase', '.temp', 'project-ref')`. If it is missing, exit with 'run supabase link first'. Pass the ref to the cp child explicitly, e.g. `env: { ...process.env, SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: ref }` (the CLI reads SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID before the ref file). Keep cwd = work so the relative destination stays in the temp dir. Prove it once against the linked project with the owner (P11).
fixCorrections: Keep cwd=work. Do not use --workdir repoRoot, because the CLI would chdir and could resolve the relative destination inside the repo. For '--linked', use process.env.SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID if it is set. Otherwise read join(repoRoot,'supabase','.temp','project-ref'), and if that is missing, exit before any dump with 'run supabase link first'. Pass the ref only to the cp child: supabase([...], { cwd: work, env: { ...process.env, SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: ref } }). Prove it once against the linked project with the owner (P11).

Keep cwd = work (passing --workdir repoRoot would chdir the CLI and land the relative destination inside the repo). For --linked, read join(repoRoot,'supabase','.temp','project-ref') once before the dumps; if missing, exit with 'run supabase link first'; pass env: { ...process.env, SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: ref } to the cp spawn only. Record the check as a P11 owner step.

The suggested fix is correct and minimal. For `--linked`, read `join(repoRoot,'supabase','.temp','project-ref')`, exit with 'run supabase link first' if it is missing, and pass `env: { ...process.env, SUPABASE_PROJECT_ID: ref }` only to the cp spawn, keeping `cwd: work`. Do not use `--workdir repoRoot`: the CLI would chdir there, and the relative `storage/<bucket>` destination would land inside the repo. The one-time proof against the hosted project stays with the owner in P11.

confirmed.title: The reader rejects a valid backup whose last entry is zero bytes (`Entry data is truncated`), so the file can never be extracted or rehearsed
confirmed.failureScenario: openEntry sets state 'data' with sizeLeft 0 for an empty file. The entry is closed only after at least one more data byte arrives, because of the `data.length === 0` break. When the empty file is the last entry, no bytes follow, and _final (line 317) sees state 'data' and throws CORRUPT 'Entry data is truncated.' cleanupExtracted then deletes everything. How it happens: `.emptyFolderPlaceholder` objects are 0 bytes (Studio creates one per folder), and a 0-byte quarantine part is possible. With a Studio-created folder that sorts after `m/` in media-public, or with media-public empty and a 0-byte object last in media-private (or any order on macOS APFS), backup.mjs reports «Backup written», but both `restore-check` modes fail and the owner cannot get the dumps back out of the file. The unit test's empty.txt is never the last entry, so it passes.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In EntryExtractor.consume's data branch, close a finished entry before the empty-data break: `if (this.sizeLeft === 0) { await this.closeEntry(); continue }` placed ahead of `if (data.length === 0) break`. Add one unit case in tests/unit/backup-format.test.ts whose last entry is an empty file.
reasons: CONFIRM: In backup-format.mjs:384-387 openEntry sets sizeLeft=0/state='data' for an empty entry, and the data branch at :340 breaks on empty input before :349 can close it, so an empty entry is closed only when a following byte arrives; as the final entry no bytes follow and _final (:317) throws CORRUPT, then cleanupExtracted wipes the output. backup.mjs:187 appends walkFiles(storage) entries last with no size filter, so a 0-byte object (e.g. a folder placeholder) sorting last makes a written backup unreadable; the unit test's empty.txt (backup-format.test.ts:48) is not last.

confirmed.title: `restore-check --extract` writes the decrypted plaintext (auth users, TOTP secrets, customer data) into any directory, including inside the repository
confirmed.failureScenario: pnpm runs scripts with cwd = the package root. So when the owner follows docs/operations.md:513 from the project folder with `pnpm restore-check <file> --extract restore`, the files go to <repo>/restore/. That folder then holds roles.sql, data.sql (auth.users password hashes, auth.mfa_factors TOTP secrets, contacts, orders) and every original image in plaintext. .gitignore does not exclude them, so a later `git add -A` and push publishes them. backup.mjs:46-52 refuses this exact mistake for the encrypted file ('A backup inside the repository could be committed by accident'), but the far more sensitive plaintext has no such guard.

fixCorrections: The suggested guard is right, but restore-check.mjs:24 imports only dirname/join/resolve from node:path, so add `relative` and `isAbsolute` to that import. Apply the guard in main() before readBackup (or at arg parse, next to line 50), copying backup.mjs's check.
reasons: CONFIRM: scripts/restore-check.mjs:308-310 resolves --extract with no location check, and package.json:30 runs it via pnpm with cwd at the repo root, so a relative dir lands in the repo; .gitignore has no rule covering it. backup.mjs:46-52 refuses exactly this for the encrypted --out, so the inconsistency is unintended, and neither ISSUES.md nor DECISIONS.md records it. confirmed.title: A transient current_staff_role() failure (including on every tab refocus) switches the whole admin to «لا تملك صلاحية الوصول» and unmounts the open screen

Each of these events re-runs evaluate(). Example: the owner is typing in the invite form, the commerce seller form or a document editor, and the laptop sleeps. On wake the tab becomes visible before Wi-Fi is back, so the RPC fails with a fetch error. The gate drops from 'ready' to 'no-role', the children unmount and anything not yet autosaved is lost. The owner then sees 'you do not have access' plus a sign-out button, although his role never changed. The same wrong message appears on first load whenever the network fails.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In AdminShell.evaluate, tell an RPC error apart from a null role and never downgrade a ready gate on an error: `if (error) { setGate((prev) => (prev.status === 'ready' ? prev : { status: 'no-role' })); return }` and keep `if (!data) setGate({ status: 'no-role' })` for a real missing role.
fixCorrections: The suggested fix is right as the minimal change: on an RPC error, keep a 'ready' gate as it is, and use no-role only when data is null. On first load an error still falls through to the misleading «لا تملك صلاحية الوصول». Optionally add an error state or a retry, or at least avoid showing the no-access message when `error` is set.
reasons: CONFIRM: AdminShell.tsx:43 handles `error || !data` as 'no-role'. Periodic TOKEN_REFRESHED events also re-run it, so one failed fetch after wake or a network blip wipes the open screen. confirmed.title: Selectable text layer is offset from the drawn words by the 4:5 frame's origin (selection and find land on the wrong lines)
confirmed.failureScenario: The canvas is drawn through the frame (offsetX/offsetY shift the ink by -frame.x/-frame.y), but pdf.js 6's TextLayer ignores viewport offsets. It places spans at full-A4 coordinates, as percentages of a container sized to var(--total-scale-factor) * 595x842, anchored at the leaf's top. For the shipped preview the text block gives frame.y of about 36pt (pypdf bbox: text y 72 to 758 on an 842pt page), so every invisible span sits about 36*scale px below its ink. In «عرض للقراءة» at 880px that is about 53px, roughly two lines at Word's 12pt. With RTL right-anchoring the layer is also shifted a few px horizontally. A reader who drags across a drawn line in the reading view (the view the reader offers for selecting) selects and copies text from other lines. Ctrl+F highlights appear below the matching words. The layer (842*scale tall) also runs past the 4:5 sheet (757*scale) and covers the sheet label under it. No e2e checks span-to-ink alignment; reader.spec.ts only checks the layer's textContent.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In pdf.ts, build the text layer with an unshifted viewport and move its container by the frame instead: `this.layer = new pdfjs.TextLayer({ textContentSource: content, container: this.text, viewport: page.getViewport({ scale }) })`, then `Object.assign(this.text.style, { left: `${-frame.x * scale}px`, top: `${-frame.y * scale}px`, right: 'auto', bottom: 'auto' })`. Add `overflow: clip` to `.sheet` in reader.module.css (`.leaf` already hides overflow). One e2e check: in the reading view, the first span's rect sits inside the sheet near the top text line.
fixCorrections: Suggested fix is right: build the TextLayer from page.getViewport({ scale }) (no offsets) and position the container with inline left = -frame.x*scale px, top = -frame.y*scale px, right/bottom auto (inline styles override the CSS inset:0; width/height stay from setLayerDimensions). Add overflow: clip to .sheet (the .leaf already has overflow: hidden). Optional e2e: first span rect inside the sheet near the first ink line.

Suggested fix is correct. Build the layer with `page.getViewport({ scale })` and set inline `left: ${-frame.x*scale}px; top: ${-frame.y*scale}px; right: auto; bottom: auto` on this.text. `right: auto` is required, because in RTL the over-constrained box otherwise ignores `left`. Add `overflow: clip` to `.sheet`; `.leaf` already has `overflow: hidden`. Add one e2e assertion that the first span's rect falls inside the sheet near the first drawn line.

The suggested fix is correct. Build the TextLayer with `page.getViewport({ scale })` (no offset). Then set `this.text.style` to left `${-frame.x*scale}px`, top `${-frame.y*scale}px`, right 'auto', bottom 'auto'. Setting right to auto is required, or RTL over-constraint ignores left. Add `overflow: clip` to `.sheet`; `.leaf` already hides overflow. It applies to both callers (StaticPdfReader and PdfBookReader), because both go through PageSurface.draw.
reasons: CONFIRM: pdf.ts:151/181 passes a viewport shifted by offsetX/offsetY to TextLayer, but pdf.js 6.3.289 TextLayer (pdf.mjs ~15093-15099) builds its transform only from viewport.rawDims (the viewBox, no offsets) and setLayerDimensions sizes the layer to the full A4 pageWidth/pageHeight, so spans sit at A4 coordinates while the canvas ink is drawn shifted by -frame.x/-frame.y. reader.module.css:323-328 anchors the layer with inset:0 (right-anchored in RTL once width is inline-set) and .sheet (css ~542) has no overflow clipping, so the A4-tall layer overhangs the 4:5 sheet; nothing in ISSUES/DESIGN-AUDIT records this and tests/e2e/reader.spec.ts does not check span-to-ink alignment. Screen readers are unaffected (reference text), so impact is selection/copy/find misplacement, medium rather than high.

CONFIRM: pdf.ts:151/181 passes the frame-offset viewport to TextLayer, but pdf.js 6.3.289 TextLayer builds its transform only from viewport.rawDims (pdf.mjs:15093-15099, rawDims = viewBox at :883-891) and sizes the container from rawDims too (setLayerDimensions :1524-1541), so offsetX/offsetY are ignored while the canvas (pdf.ts:152-155) is drawn through the frame. The .textLayer gets `inset: 0` (reader.module.css:323-327) plus inline width/height of 595x842*scale, so spans sit frame.y*scale lower than the ink (and, in the RTL containing block, the right-anchored layer is also shifted horizontally); this shared PageSurface affects both the flip leaves and the «عرض للقراءة» sheets. Nothing in PLANS/ISSUES.md, DESIGN-AUDIT.md or EXCEPTIONS.md records it, and reader.spec.ts:175-177 only checks the layer's textContent, not where it sits. Severity is medium, not high: selection and find are misplaced, but no data, security or money path is affected.

CONFIRM: src/components/book/pdf.ts:151,181 pass the offset viewport to TextLayer, but pdf.js 6.3.289 builds its transform only from viewport.rawDims, i.e. the unshifted viewBox (pdf.mjs:15093-15099, 883-891). It also sizes the layer at full A4 (setLayerDimensions, pdf.mjs:1524-1541), while reader.module.css:323-327 pins the layer with `inset: 0` inside a 4:5 `.sheet` (:542) that has no overflow clipping. So the spans sit frame.y*scale below the ink (horizontally they are right-anchored in RTL), and the layer runs past the sheet. Nothing in ISSUES.md, DESIGN-AUDIT.md, docs/book-preview.md or the P02 tasmeem FINDINGS/FIXES records this; docs/book-preview.md:95 says the layer exists for selecting and finding. confirmed.title: page-flip's requestAnimationFrame loop never stops after destroy(): each close of the book leaks a perpetual 60fps loop and the whole leaf DOM
confirmed.failureScenario: page-flip 2.0.7's Render.start() schedules requestAnimationFrame forever, and PageFlip.destroy() only removes handlers and elements; nothing cancels the loop. Each time the book effect cleans up, the old loop keeps running drawFrame() every frame on detached leaves (style.cssText writes on all 12 leaves) and holds the leaves, cover img, spoken-text divs and PageFlip instance in memory. Cleanup runs on a switch to «عرض للقراءة», on a retry, and on leaving /book by client-side navigation (RoomNav links). A reader who toggles book/reading view 5 times leaves 5 loops running on top of the live one for the rest of the SPA session. The cost is CPU and battery on phones plus a memory leak.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Patch page-flip 2.0.7 through `pnpm patch page-flip` (patchedDependencies in package.json; the bundle resolves dist/js/page-flip.browser.js via `main`). In Render.start's loop, return when a `stopped` flag is set, and make PageFlip.destroy() set `this.render.stopped = true` before `this.ui.destroy()`. The reader code stays unchanged.
reasons: CONFIRM: page-flip 2.0.7 (main = dist/js/page-flip.browser.js) has `start(){...const t=e=>{this.render(e),requestAnimationFrame(t)}...}` and `destroy(){this.ui.destroy(),this.block.remove()}`, so nothing stops the loop; HTMLRender.drawFrame/clear writes style.cssText on every page and does not throw on detached nodes, so each loop runs forever. PdfBookReader.tsx:390 cleanup runs on every mode toggle, retry and client-side unmount (the reader is lazy-loaded from BookPreview.tsx:30), so the loops pile up and keep the leaves alive. Nothing in PLANS/ISSUES.md records it.

confirmed.title: Contact textarea allows 5,000 characters, but the function rejects bodies over 8 KiB, so long Arabic messages fail after the visitor has written them
confirmed.evidence:
<textarea ... maxLength={5000}   (ContactForm.tsx:164)
vs supabase/functions/_shared/contact.ts:26-32: "Arabic is two bytes a character in UTF-8, so a message stops fitting near 4,000 Arabic characters ... the P01 form should cap its textarea accordingly." const MAX_BODY_BYTES = 8_192
confirmed.failureScenario: A visitor writes a 3,800-character Arabic message. The textarea accepts it because it is under maxLength 5000. They solve Turnstile and press أرسل. The JSON body is about 7.6 KB of message, plus the name, email, UUID and a Turnstile token of up to 2 KB, which is more than 8,192 bytes. The function answers 413 «رسالتك أطول من المسموح؛ اختصرها…». The token is spent, and the form never says how much to cut, even though the handler's comment asks the form to cap the field.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In ContactForm.tsx, cap the field to what fits in bytes. Before the fetch in submit(), add `if (new TextEncoder().encode(values.message.trim()).length > 5500) { setErrors({ message: 'رسالتك أطول من المسموح؛ اختصرها.' }); messageRef.current?.focus(); return }`, and lower maxLength to 2750. This keeps the check ahead of the Turnstile spend.
fixCorrections: Fix it once in one of two ways. (a) The root cause is that the byte ceiling is smaller than the schema's 5,000-character bound. Raise MAX_BODY_BYTES in contact.ts to 16_384 (5000×2 + 2048 token + fields fits, and the 32 KiB declared-length guard stays) and update the '8 KiB' wording in PLANS/ARCHITECTURE.md:95, docs/operations.md:42 and the contact.ts:26-31 comment. (b) If 8 KiB must stay, keep maxLength and add only the client check in submit() before the Turnstile check: if new TextEncoder().encode(values.message.trim()).length > 5500, set the message error and focus it.
reasons: CONFIRM: ContactForm.tsx:164 caps the textarea at 5000 UTF-16 units, while contact.ts:32/130 refuses bodies over 8,192 bytes; at 2 bytes per Arabic character plus a token of up to 2,048 bytes (contact.ts:96), a message of roughly 3,000 or more Arabic characters gets a 413 after the Turnstile token is spent (the finally block at ContactForm.tsx:101 resets it). The handler's own comment (contact.ts:26-30) asks the P01 form to cap the field, and PLANS/ISSUES.md does not record it. The suggested fix stacks two mechanisms: maxLength 2750 and a 5500-byte check are redundant, and 2750 halves the limit for Latin-script writers.

confirmed.title: Storage-denied cart: edits made on /cart never reach the memory cart, so /checkout shows and orders the stale cart
confirmed.failureScenario: The browser blocks storage (for example Chrome with all cookies blocked), so cartArea() returns null and readCart() returns the module-level memoryCart with persistent:false. The buyer adds A x1 and B x1 on the product page, which updates memoryCart through AddToCart's writeCart. On /cart they remove B and set A to 3. Because previous.persistent is false, the `&&` short-circuits and writeCart is never called, so memoryCart still holds [A x1, B x1]. The buyer presses «المتابعة لإتمام الطلب», a next/link client navigation that keeps module state. The checkout page's new CartProvider calls readCart() and gets [A x1, B x1], so the summary shows the removed line and the old quantity, and `create` orders them. The same thing happens after one setItem fails mid-session (quota): later edits are never written and the next page reads the older localStorage cart. This breaks DATA-AND-SECURITY 'Checkout transaction' step 1: 'Storage denial still permits session cart.'
confirmed.suggestedFix: In src/components/store/CartProvider.tsx, always write and keep the flag sticky: `const update = useCallback((next: CartV1) => { const saved = writeCart(next); setState((previous) => ({ cart: next, persistent: (previous?.persistent ?? true) && saved })) }, [])`. writeCart already updates memoryCart when storage is denied or throws. This also moves the side effect out of the state updater.
fixCorrections: The suggested fix is correct and minimal for the storage-denied case: `const saved = writeCart(next); setState((previous) => ({ cart: next, persistent: (previous?.persistent ?? true) && saved }))`. It does not cover the mid-session quota failure the finding also names. There, cartArea() is non-null, so the next page's readCart reads the older localStorage value, not memoryCart. That case is practically unreachable for a tiny ID/quantity cart, so leave it or note it with a ponytail comment.

The suggested fix is correct for the storage-denied case: call writeCart(next) outside the updater on every update, and AND the result into a sticky flag. It only partly fixes the quota case: readCart (cart.ts:234-247) prefers localStorage whenever getItem works, so a cart that failed setItem is still read back stale on the next page. To close that too, have readCart return memoryCart when a write has failed in this tab (for example a module-level `writeFailed` flag set in writeCart's catch).

confirmed.title: A Resend daily or monthly quota 429 counts as a bounded retry, so notices are exhausted about 4 hours later, long before the quota resets
confirmed.evidence: if (status === 429) return { outcome: 'retry', error: 'RATE_LIMIT' }

But outbox_result (migration 20260926120000 lines 351-364) gives a retry a backoff of 2^attempts minutes: 2+4+...+128, about 254 minutes in total. The 8th claim then marks the row exhausted. The outbox counts only its own sent rows, while Resend also counts sign-in codes sent over SMTP. So Resend's daily_quota_exceeded or monthly_quota_exceeded can arrive while the outbox's own count is still under its cap. Example: Resend's day fills at 12:00 UTC. Every notice claimed after that gets 429 and is exhausted by about 16:15 UTC, with an email.exhausted audit row. runOutbox also keeps claiming up to 10 rows per run, so each waiting row burns attempts. The notices never go out unless someone replays each row from البريد. With the monthly quota, every notice until the month ends is exhausted.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In email.ts, return error 'QUOTA' when the 429 body name is daily_quota_exceeded or monthly_quota_exceeded, and keep 'RATE_LIMIT' for rate_limit_exceeded. In a new migration, `create or replace public.outbox_result` so that when p_outcome='retry' and p_error='QUOTA' the row goes back to status 'pending' with `attempts = o.attempts - 1` and `next_at = date_trunc('day', now(), 'UTC') + interval '1 day'`. In outbox.ts runOutbox, `break` out of the claim loop after a QUOTA outcome. Functional impact: notices blocked by the quota wait for the reset and do not use up their retry budget.

The quota is reachable before the outbox's own cap: RESERVE holds back only priority 2 (outbox.ts:26-35), and D31 routes Supabase Auth SMTP codes through the same Resend quota. In the new create-or-replace of content_go_live, clear the approval only when the seq actually changes: `if p_collection = 'policies' and (select policy_revisions ->> p_doc_id from finance.commerce_settings where id = 1) is distinct from p_seq::text then update finance.commerce_settings set policy_revisions = '{}'::jsonb, version = version + 1 where id = 1; end if;`. That way republishing the approved seq does not close checkout. Also clear it when an unapproved optional doc is published, such as privacy published after approval: that doc is not a key in policy_revisions, so the `?` guard in the suggested fix would skip it, and the checkout consent sentence could link to the new privacy page while the stored approval omits it. Add an audit_events row ('commerce.policies_reset') so the owner can see why checkout closed.

Check that seed-demo-catalog.mjs:223-245 still writes policy_revisions after its content_go_live calls (it does).

confirmed.title: Claude settings allow `node dist/cli.js` with no prompt, and the graft hook falls back to importing <repo>/dist/claude/hooks.js, both copied from graft's own repository

confirmed.failureScenario: In acceptEdits mode, where edits are auto-approved, an agent steered by injected content can write dist/cli.js and then run `node dist/cli.js`. fixCorrections: Delete only the `Bash(graft-dev:*)` and `Bash(node dist/cli.js:*)` lines from .claude/settings.json (keep the preceding entry's comma correct). The graft-hooks.cjs line-64 edit is optional because it closes no new vector, and a graft re-install regenerates that file.

That contradicts ci.yml:5 and VERIFICATION.md:8 ('No masked nonzero exits'). Both directories have files today (23 and 15), so it is a latent guard gap rather than an active bug, and the flag looks like a leftover from before any tests existed.

confirmed.title: Data contract promises a NOLOGIN function-owner role that no migration creates
confirmed.evidence: Server-only functions are granted to `service_role` and revoked from `anon` and `authenticated`. A NOLOGIN function-owner role holds the narrow table rights those functions need.
confirmed.failureScenario: grep of all 14 migrations: the only `create role` is app_server (dropped by 20260927090000), there is no `owner to`, and about 57 `security definer` functions run as the migration role `postgres`. If least privilege is wanted instead, P10 adds a NOLOGIN owner role and `alter function ... owner to` it in a new migration.
reasons: CONFIRM: PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:49 promises a NOLOGIN function-owner role, but the only `create role` in the migrations is app_server (20260924130000:85), which 20260927090000:292 drops. confirmed.title: Closing the terminal window (SIGHUP on Windows) skips the 'exit' cleanup and leaves the plaintext dumps in %TEMP%
confirmed.failureScenario: The owner closes the console window during the minutes-long dump or download, or during a restore-check rehearsal. Windows sends CTRL_CLOSE_EVENT, which Node raises as SIGHUP. With no SIGHUP listener, Node terminates without emitting 'exit'. %TEMP%\anasaq-backup-* (roles/schema/data.sql with auth password hashes and TOTP secrets, plus the media originals) or %TEMP%\anasaq-restore-files-* stays on disk unencrypted indefinitely. The code comments promise 'the plaintext dumps never stay in the temp dir', and D35 relies on the file being encrypted at rest.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add `process.on('SIGHUP', () => { cleanup(); process.exit(129) })` in scripts/backup.mjs, and `process.on('SIGHUP', () => process.exit(129))` next to the SIGINT/SIGTERM handlers in scripts/restore-check.mjs. Windows allows about 10 s after a SIGHUP listener runs, which is enough for rmSync.
fixCorrections: In backup.mjs, add process.on('SIGHUP', () => { cleanup(); process.exit(129) }). In restore-check.mjs, add process.on('SIGHUP', () => process.exit(129)). Also move rmSync(extractDir) (and rmSync of scratch) ahead of the `supabase stop` call in cleanup at restore-check.mjs:~327. That stop call can take up to 300 s, well past Windows' ~10 s post-SIGHUP window, so the decrypted dumps must be removed first.
reasons: CONFIRM: backup.mjs:113-121 and restore-check.mjs:333,408-409 handle only 'exit', SIGINT and SIGTERM. On Windows, closing the console raises SIGHUP, and with no listener Node's default action terminates the process without emitting 'exit', so %TEMP%\anasaq-backup-* (plaintext dumps) or anasaq-restore-files-* is left on disk. No SIGHUP handling is recorded in PLANS/ISSUES.md.

confirmed.title: writeBackup adds one 'error' listener to the framing stream per entry, so every real backup prints a MaxListenersExceededWarning 'memory leak' notice
confirmed.failureScenario: Each writeEntryHeader call adds a never-removed `framing.once('error', ...)`, and writeEntryBytes adds another. The P06 backup had 227 entries, which means about 229 listeners on one PassThrough. Past 10, Node prints to stderr in the middle of the owner's backup: '(node:…) MaxListenersExceededWarning: Possible EventEmitter memory leak detected. 11 error listeners added to [PassThrough]'. That reads like the backup is broken, and the listeners grow linearly with the object count.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In writeBackup, create one `const framingFailed = failurePromise(framing)` next to outFailed. Pass it to writeEntryBytes and writeEntryHeader instead of creating a new failure promise in each call.
reasons: CONFIRM: writeEntryHeader (:197) and writeEntryBytes (:178) each call failurePromise(framing), which adds a framing.once('error') (:79) that stays attached until an error happens, so the count grows by one per entry. With more than 10 entries (backup.mjs:181-188 adds one per storage object), Node prints MaxListenersExceededWarning to stderr. It is cosmetic and does not corrupt the backup, but it looks alarming.

confirmed.title: The hidden prompt drops only the ESC byte of arrow, Home and Delete key sequences and adds their tails (e.g. "[D", "[3~") to the passphrase
confirmed.failureScenario: In raw mode, Windows (libuv) and Unix terminals deliver Left-arrow as "\x1b[D" and Delete as "\x1b[3~". The loop skips \x1b but pushes '[' and 'D'. Suppose the owner, typing blind, presses Left-arrow to fix a typo while entering the passphrase for `pnpm restore-check`. The derived key is then for 'secret[D...' and he gets 'Decryption failed: wrong passphrase or damaged file' for a correct file. At backup time the result is either a confusing mismatch, or, if the same keys are pressed in both prompts, a stored passphrase he can never retype. The comment claims these sequences are excluded; the code does not exclude them.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In promptHidden, when '\u001b' is seen, skip the whole sequence: set a flag, ignore an optional '[' or 'O' and any parameter bytes, and clear the flag on the final byte (a character in '@'..'~'). Keep everything else as is.
fixCorrections: Same approach, but keep the escape state in the promptHidden closure next to `characters`, not inside the loop, so a sequence split across two 'data' chunks is still skipped. On '\u001b' set state=1. In state 1, '[' or 'O' moves to state 2; any other character ends the sequence and is dropped (this covers Alt+key). In state 2, drop parameter and intermediate bytes (0x20-0x3F) and clear the state on a final byte in '@'..'~'. Leave everything else unchanged, and add one small assert check that feeds 'ab\x1b[Dc\x1b[3~d\x1bOA' through the handler and expects 'abcd'.
reasons: CONFIRM: scripts/lib/passphrase.mjs:33 drops only C0/C1 control characters, so for a raw-mode Left arrow "\x1b[D" or Delete "\x1b[3~" the loop at :24 skips ESC and pushes '[', 'D' (or '[', '3', '~'), which contradicts the comment at :31-32. The prompt is used by scripts/backup.mjs:75-76 (entered twice, compared) and scripts/restore-check.mjs:78, so an arrow key pressed while typing blind silently changes the derived key. Nothing in PLANS/ISSUES.md records it. Impact is limited: the backup case either mismatches or stores tails that the same keystrokes reproduce, and restore fails loudly rather than corrupting data.

confirmed.title: The idempotency key lives only in memory, so after a lost response and a reload the buyer is blocked by their own hold and told to do something the page cannot do
confirmed.failureScenario: create reaches the server and the order commits, but the response is lost, so the UI shows «تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة؛ أعد المحاولة.». The buyer reloads, which is a common reaction, and the ref-held key and fingerprint are gone. The next identical submit mints a new key. checkout_create finds the unexpired hold for this email or session and answers ACTIVE_HOLD. readPendingOrder() is null because the token never arrived, so the buyer sees «لديك طلب قيد الانتظار؛ أكمله أو ألغه أولًا.». The page offers no way to complete or cancel that order, and the buyer is blocked for up to 20 minutes. The DATA contract says same-request retries reuse the original order; with the key held only in memory, that stops working after a reload.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Persist the pair {fingerprint, idempotencyKey} with writeSessionValue under a new key in src/lib/cart.ts, and read it back in the mount effect. A reload-and-retry of the identical request then reuses the key, and the server returns the duplicate order with its access token.
reasons: CONFIRM: The idempotency key and fingerprint live only in refs (CheckoutForm.tsx:85-86). The checkout session persists in sessionStorage (cart.ts:302-307), and the email-or-session hold check runs after the idempotency lookup (migration:837 vs 886-893). So after a lost response and a reload, a new key hits ACTIVE_HOLD. readPendingOrder() is null because the token never arrived, and the page offers no way to complete or cancel the order. The suggested fix works: the access token is derived from pepper and idempotencyKey (checkout.ts:149, 355), and a duplicate returns it when the hash matches (checkout.ts:376-377). Nothing in ISSUES.md records this.

confirmed.title: Server field errors (422 INVALID) are dropped, so a rejected email shows only «بيانات غير صالحة.»
confirmed.evidence: setSubmitError(error?.message ?? 'تعذّر إتمام الطلب.')
confirmed.failureScenario: The buyer types 'name@gmail.c'. The client regex /^[^@\s]+@[^@\s]+\.[^@\s]+$/ accepts it, but the server's EMAIL_SHAPE needs a TLD of at least 2 letters, so the function answers 422 {code:'INVALID', fields:{fieldErrors:{email:['بريد غير صالح.']}}}. CheckoutForm ignores fields.fieldErrors and shows the generic banner 'بيانات غير صالحة.'. The email field gets no aria-invalid or focus, so the buyer cannot tell what to fix. The same happens for a name over 120 characters (the input has no maxLength).
confirmed.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.submit, when `error?.code === 'INVALID'`, map `error.fields?.fieldErrors` keys that match the Field names (email, name, phone, address) into setErrors with their messages, and focus the first one, before falling back to setSubmitError.
fixCorrections: Map error.fields.fieldErrors keys that are Field names into setErrors and focus the first one, as suggested. Also add maxLength={120} to the name input and tighten the client email regex to require a TLD of at least 2 characters, so the common cases are caught before the request.
reasons: CONFIRM: The server's EMAIL_SHAPE (supabase/functions/_shared/contact.ts:59) needs a TLD of at least 2 letters, and name is limited to max(120) (_shared/checkout.ts:81). A failed parse returns 422 INVALID with parsed.error.flatten() (checkout.ts:261), and a bad phone returns fieldErrors.phone (checkout.ts:319). CheckoutForm.tsx:292 shows only error.message and never reads fields.fieldErrors, even though quote.ts:209 already types fieldErrors. Recoverable, but the buyer is not told which field is wrong.

confirmed.title: A duplicate `create` reply for an expired or cancelled order is shown as a live 20-minute hold
confirmed.failureScenario: The first `create` commits but the response is lost, so the form shows 'تعذّر الاتصال بالخدمة'. The buyer comes back 25 minutes later and presses «تأكيد الطلب» with the same fields, which reuses the same idempotency key. checkout_create answers duplicate:true with the order that checkout_expire has since marked 'expired'. The client never reads order.status, so it saves the pending order and shows 'حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة', but the hold and its stock were already released.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.submit after parsing, if `order.status === 'expired' || order.status === 'cancelled'`, call setClosed(order.status) (and still set pending so the closed view renders) instead of presenting a live hold.
fixCorrections: After orderSchema.parse, if order.status is 'expired' or 'cancelled', do not call writePendingOrder. Set pending, which the closed view needs, and call setClosed(order.status), so the stale token never reaches sessionStorage.
reasons: CONFIRM: checkout_create returns duplicate:true with the current order_summary whatever its state (migrations/20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:837-848), and the checkout-expire cron marks lapsed holds 'expired' every minute (:1082, :1093). The edge function then returns the same deterministic accessToken (checkout.ts:149, 376-377). CheckoutForm.tsx:259-266 never reads order.status (it is parsed at quote.ts:177), so it shows «حُجز طلبك لمدة 20 دقيقة». The narrow path needs a lost response plus a retry after 20 minutes, and pressing cancel then correctly shows 'expired'.

confirmed.title: Submit is not blocked while the quote is stale or refused, so avoidable refusals use up the buyer's five hourly create attempts
confirmed.evidence:
if (!quote || !cart || submitting) return
...
quoteHash: quote.quoteHash,
confirmed.failureScenario: (1) With a physical cart, the buyer picks a city and presses «تأكيد الطلب» before the 300 ms debounce and the quote round trip finish. create sends the new cityKey with the old city-less quoteHash. The server re-prices with the city and answers QUOTE_CHANGED «تغيّر السعر أو التوفر…», although nothing changed. (2) With quote.ok=false (OUT_OF_STOCK, COUPON_INVALID), the button stays enabled, and every press spends a Turnstile token and one attempt from the per-email throttle (5 per hour, taken at line 880 before re-pricing). After five presses, the buyer who then fixes the cart gets RATE_LIMITED for up to an hour.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In CheckoutForm.tsx, track a `quoting` flag: set it when the debounced quote effect schedules a fetch, clear it when the fetch settles, and disable the submit while it is true. In submit(), return early with setSubmitError('راجع ملخص الطلب أولًا.') when !quote.ok.
fixCorrections: Don't call a synchronous setQuoting in the effect body: the code avoids that on purpose (react-hooks/set-state-in-effect, lines 90-91, 111). Instead, store the quote with the inputs that produced it: build `key = JSON.stringify([toApiLines(cart.lines), city, coupon])` in the effect and in refreshQuote, and call setQuote with that key. Treat the quote as stale when its key differs from the current one. Disable submit and return early when the quote is stale or `!quote.ok` (setSubmitError('راجع ملخص الطلب أولًا.')).
reasons: CONFIRM: submit() only checks `!quote || !cart || submitting` (CheckoutForm.tsx:198), and the button is disabled only for siteKey, submitting or awaitingToken (608), so a quote with ok=false or a stale quote still posts. In 20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:879-881, the per-email throttle (5 per hour) is taken before re-pricing (911-917). A refusal returns jsonb and commits, so the attempt stays counted. Case 1 needs the buyer to press within the 300 ms debounce plus the round trip; case 2 needs repeated presses. So the harm is real but narrow.

confirmed.title: One page at a time, the canvas window ignores skipped blank/endpaper leaves, so a turn between parts reveals an empty page
confirmed.failureScenario: On a phone (portrait) at «الإهداء» (leaf 2), renderWindow gives {1,2,3}, and leaves 1 and 3 are the endpaper and a blank. «التالية», ← or a tap runs turn(), which skips the blank and calls go(4) (the first page of «المقدمة»). Leaf 4 has no canvas, so the 900ms turn reveals plain paper. The ink appears only after the 'flip' event updates the index and the page renders. Going back from leaf 4 to leaf 2 fails the same way. docs/book-preview.md promises «a turning page is never blank».
confirmed.suggestedFix: In portrait, take the neighbours past empty leaves. Give renderWindow an optional `leaves` argument and, when portrait, step first-1 and last+1 past leaves whose kind is 'blank' or 'endpaper' (the same test as `empty` in PdfBookReader). Pass `leaves` from the state effect at PdfBookReader.tsx:417.
reasons: CONFIRM: With the 5-page manifest, leafPlan gives cover0, endpaper1, page1@2, blank3, page2@4, and so on; in portrait, renderWindow(2) is {1,2,3}, and the effect at PdfBookReader.tsx:417-421 clears every other surface, so leaf 4 never has a canvas while the reader sits on 2. turn(1) skips the blank and calls go(4) (PdfBookReader.tsx:203-204). page-flip's flipToPage sets the spread next to the target and flips one page, which reveals leaf 4 while the page turns, and 'flip' (which fires updatePageIndex, then setIndex) only runs at the end, so the page is drawn late and the promise at docs/book-preview.md:68 is broken (the same happens going back from 4 to 2). The suggested fix is the right root cause: take the neighbours past empty leaves in renderWindow, and add a portrait case to tests/unit/reader-mapping.test.ts.

confirmed.title: A failed cart write is kept in memory but never read back while localStorage is readable, so AddToCart reports an item added that the cart never shows
confirmed.failureScenario: localStorage is readable but setItem throws (QuotaExceededError). writeCart stores the new cart in memoryCart and returns false. AddToCart ignores that return value and shows «أُضيف إلى السلة». On /cart, readCart() finds a non-null area and returns the stored cart without the new line, with persistent=true. The item is gone, and the «السلة مؤقتة…» note never appears.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In src/lib/cart.ts, record a module-level `writeFailed = true` in writeCart's catch. In readCart, return { cart: memoryCart, persistent: false } when writeFailed is set, before reading storage.
reasons: CONFIRM: writeCart's catch (cart.ts:262-264) stores the cart in memoryCart, but readCart (cart.ts:233-247) reads memoryCart only when the area is null or getItem throws. A setItem-only failure therefore loses the AddToCart write (AddToCart.tsx:24 ignores the return value) and shows persistent=true. This is reachable only when getItem works and setItem throws (quota full, or legacy Safari private mode), which is rare on an origin that stores a few small keys.

confirmed.title: The dedication text is saved to localStorage on every keystroke and never cleared, against DATA step 1 and P07's 'persist cart IDs/qty only'
confirmed.evidence:
cart.ts:5-7: localStorage holds `anasaq:cart:v1` ... `{ "variantId": uuid, "quantity": 1..20, "dedication"?: string }`
cart.ts:72: return JSON.stringify({ version: 1, lines: cart.lines })
cart.ts:260: area.setItem(CART_STORAGE_KEY, serializeCart(cart))
CartView.tsx:198: onChange={(event) => update(setDedication(cart, line.variantId, event.target.value))}
DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:57: "Browser stores only variant IDs, quantities and cart schema version in localStorage."
confirmed.failureScenario: A buyer on a shared family or office computer types «إلى سارة، مع كل الحب» as a signed-copy dedication on /cart. Each keystroke is written to localStorage['anasaq:cart:v1']. The cart is deliberately kept after the hold is created (CheckoutForm: nothing settles before P08), so the text stays in the browser forever. The next person who opens /cart on that device sees it. The plan's contract allows only ids, quantities and the schema version in localStorage (DATA step 1, WORK-PACKAGES P07 line 93).

Keep dedications in sessionStorage under a new key `anasaq:dedications` ({variantId: text}), using the readSessionValue/writeSessionValue helpers the file already has. readCart merges them back. The feature is unchanged within the tab: the dedication survives a reload and the cart-to-checkout step, but is gone when the tab closes. Update the matching sentence in docs/operations.md (line 426).
fixCorrections: First decide which side is authoritative. If the plan wins, apply the suggested sessionStorage split, and merge the dedications back in both readCart branches: the storage branch and the memoryCart fallback. Otherwise, amend DATA-AND-SECURITY.md step 1 and WORK-PACKAGES P07 to allow a bounded dedication in the cart. Either way, fix S06.2 in the same change.
reasons: CONFIRM: PLANS/DATA-AND-SECURITY.md:57 ('only variant IDs, quantities and cart schema version in localStorage') and WORK-PACKAGES.md:93 ('Persist cart IDs/qty only') conflict with cart.ts:5-7/72/260, which persists the free-text dedication through CartView.tsx:198 on every keystroke. The P07 brief (artifacts/acceptance/P07/brief-r3-store-pages.md:75) and docs/operations.md:426 knowingly specified dedication in localStorage, so this is an unreconciled plan-versus-implementation divergence, not an accident. The privacy impact is small (short gift text on a shared device), and nothing in DECISIONS or ISSUES records the deviation.

confirmed.title: The local-database guard checks the URL's hostname, but `pg` connects to the `?host=` query parameter
confirmed.failureScenario: Setup: TEST_ENV=local and DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pw@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres?host=db.<ref>.supabase.co. assertLocalTestDatabase passes because `new URL(...).hostname` is '127.0.0.1'. Every integration test builds `new pg.Client({ connectionString: process.env.DATABASE_URL })`, and that parser takes host from the query parameter, so `pnpm test:db` runs its destructive fixtures (for example the last-owner test that deactivates owners) against the hosted database. The guard exists to prevent exactly this data loss. tests/unit/env.test.ts has no query-parameter case, so nothing catches it.

Add one case to the isLocalDatabaseUrl block in tests/unit/env.test.ts: 'postgres://u:p@127.0.0.1:5432/db?host=db.example.com' is false.
fixCorrections: Reject any URL with a `host` search param in all three guards. In src/lib/env.ts isLocalDatabaseUrl add `if (parsed.searchParams.has('host')) return false` (a `hostaddr` check is harmless but pg ignores hostaddr). Add the same `|| parsed.searchParams.has('host')` to the refusal condition in scripts/import-content.mjs:31 and scripts/seed-demo-catalog.mjs:25. Add one false case to tests/unit/env.test.ts.
reasons: CONFIRM: src/lib/env.ts:26 checks only `new URL(url).hostname`, while pg-connection-string 2.14.0 (index.js:40-56) copies every search param into config and only falls back to the URL hostname when `config.host` is unset, so `?host=remote` bypasses the guard that vitest.config.ts calls before `pnpm test:db`. The same bypass exists in scripts/import-content.mjs:31 and scripts/seed-demo-catalog.mjs:25. It only happens with a deliberately unusual URL (an accidental `?host=` is unlikely), so this is defense-in-depth and low severity rather than medium.

confirmed.title: Media-id lookups put every id in one GET URL; at about 420 post covers the build fails with 414
confirmed.failureScenario: Each UUID adds about 39 URL characters once URLSearchParams encodes the comma as %2C. The GET answers 414, mediaById throws 'Failed to fetch media: 414', and from then on every publish fails the site build. VERIFICATION.md:55 names 500 posts as the representative load. content.ts resolveMedia and store.ts resolveCovers repeat the same single-request pattern.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Move the lookup into one helper in src/lib/content.ts that fetches ids in chunks of about 100 and merges the maps. Use it from journal.ts mediaById and store.ts resolveCovers instead of their two copies.
fixCorrections: Fix together with X6.13. Export one `mediaById(ids)` from content.ts that splits the ids into chunks of about 100, runs the GETs, and merges the rows into one Map. reasons: CONFIRM: All three loaders send every id in one PostgREST `in.(...)` GET with no chunking (journal.ts:45, content.ts:85, store.ts:76), and journal.ts:67 collects the covers of every visible post, so the URL length grows with the post count. The ~39 chars per id (36-char UUID plus %2C) put the break near 420 posts, and a non-OK answer throws, which fails the build (journal.ts:49). VERIFICATION.md:55 requires a representative 500-post load, so this is in scope. It is latent at today's volumes, so low.

confirmed.title: The contact name accepts newlines, so a visitor can forge the notice's own الاسم / البريد / الوقت lines

confirmed.failureScenario:

confirmed.title: Public functions read the whole body into memory before checking its size; boundedText() exists for this but nothing calls it
confirmed.failureScenario: An unauthenticated client POSTs a chunked body with no Content-Length to /functions/v1/contact, /checkout or /resend-webhook (all verify_jwt=false), with the correct content type and a 100 MB payload. The declared-length check sees NaN and passes. `request.text()` then buffers all 100 MB, and TextEncoder copies it again, before the 8-64 KiB limit is enforced. Repeated requests can hit the Edge Function memory limit (the worker is killed) and burn invocations on the public endpoints. The comments call the post-read check a 'backstop', but it does not bound memory.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Make http.ts boundedText stream the body. Read `request.body.getReader()`, add up `value.byteLength`, and call `reader.cancel()` and return null as soon as the total passes maxBytes. At the end, decode the collected bytes with TextDecoder, which gives the same UTF-8 text as request.text(), so the Svix signature over the raw body is unchanged. Then replace the three `await request.text()` plus post-check blocks in contact.ts:129, checkout.ts:249 and resend-webhook.ts:121 with `const text = await boundedText(request, MAX_BODY_BYTES); if (text === null) return <existing 413>`. This also removes the dead export. Functional impact: none for real requests.
fixCorrections: Stream inside boundedText in http.ts. Use `request.body?.getReader()`, sum `value.byteLength`, and call `reader.cancel()` and return null once the total exceeds maxBytes. Concatenate the chunks and decode them with `new TextDecoder().decode(...)` (non-fatal, so the output is identical to request.text()). contact.ts and checkout.ts can then switch to `const text = await boundedText(request, MAX_BODY_BYTES); if (text === null) return fail(413, ...)`. That leaves checkout's MAX_DECLARED_BODY_BYTES and contact's 32 KiB declared pre-check redundant; drop them. resend-webhook.ts still needs `bodyBytes` for the MAX_EVENT_BYTES branch at :164, so keep `const bodyBytes = new TextEncoder().encode(rawBody).length` after the bounded read, or have the helper return the byte count too. admin.ts:135 and jobs.ts:36 have the same unbounded read but sit behind a JWT or a secret; routing them through the helper is optional.
reasons: CONFIRM: The code matches the finding. contact.ts:124-130, checkout.ts:244-250 and resend-webhook.ts:113-122 only check Content-Length, which is NaN on a chunked request, then call `await request.text()`, so the whole body is buffered before the byte check. All three endpoints are verify_jwt=false (config.toml:413-424), and their pre-read gates (the Origin header, the content type, a configured secret) are trivially satisfied by a non-browser client. Severity stays low: Supabase's platform memory and wall-clock limits cap the damage to one killed worker and wasted invocations, with no data exposure.

confirmed.title: A failed staff-row lookup is reported as unauthenticated, so the owner is told the page is for owners only
confirmed.failureScenario: A transient PostgREST or database error on the staff lookup, after the token has already been verified as genuine, returns null. The admin function answers 401 UNAUTHENTICATED. On /admin/stats the signed-in owner then reads that statistics are for the owner only, instead of 'failed, reload'. The media and commerce screens get an auth error for what is a server fault. The module's own contract (line 6) says null means 'a missing, bad or unverifiable token', not a database failure.

fixCorrections: A bare throw escapes handleAdmin, because admin/index.ts is just Deno.serve(handleAdmin). Deno's default handler then answers a plain-text 500 with no CORS headers. The browser sees a CORS failure: it still ends up as UNKNOWN, but it breaks the function's JSON and CORS contract. Throw in staff.ts:37 as suggested, and also wrap the lookup in handleAdmin (admin.ts:132): `let staff; try { staff = await deps.staff(request) } catch { return fail(500, 'FAILED', 'تعذّر إكمال الإجراء.') }`. The reply then carries CORS headers and JSON. Add one unit case in tests/unit/admin-function.test.ts with a resolver that throws, expecting a 500.
reasons: CONFIRM: supabase/functions/_shared/staff.ts:37 returns null on a staff query error, which contradicts its own contract at line 6. handleAdmin turns null into 401 UNAUTHENTICATED (supabase/functions/_shared/admin.ts:133), and StatsView.tsx:53 maps that to the owner-only message. It is reachable only on a transient PostgREST or DB fault after a valid token, so it stays low.

confirmed.title: When a restore's ban lift fails, the message says sign-in could not be stopped, and the member is left shown as active while still banned

confirmed.title: The default-privilege revoke of EXECUTE from PUBLIC does nothing, so functions are not deny-by-default
confirmed.evidence:
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public
  revoke execute on functions from public, anon, authenticated;
confirmed.failureScenario: Postgres cannot revoke per schema a privilege that is granted globally: the built-in EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC default is global. PUBLIC therefore keeps EXECUTE on every new function, and anon and authenticated inherit it through PUBLIC. If a future migration adds `create function public.x() ... security definer` without its own `revoke ... from public`, anon can call it at /rest/v1/rpc/x (has_function_privilege('anon','public.x()','execute') = true). That contradicts the file's comment "Deny by default ... each object is granted explicitly" and DATA-AND-SECURITY's "Revoke PUBLIC function execution". Nothing is exposed today: every current function revokes from public explicitly (checked across all 14 migrations).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a new migration with `alter default privileges for role postgres revoke execute on functions from public;` (global, with no `in schema`), which also covers `finance`. Functional impact: none, because every existing function already grants its callers explicitly.
reasons: CONFIRM: 20260924130000_staff_and_app_server.sql:11-12 revokes per schema (`in schema public`), and Postgres documents that a per-schema REVOKE cannot remove a global default. The built-in EXECUTE-to-PUBLIC default therefore still applies to every new function, which contradicts the 'Deny by default' comment at lines 5-6. Nothing is exposed today: I compared function creates with revokes in every migration, and each new function revokes explicitly, while the create-or-replace redefinitions (outbox_kick, media_is_published, media_delete) keep their existing ACLs. The gap is latent hardening, so low severity is right.

confirmed.title: Anonymous media reads run media_is_published once per row, a full JSON-path scan of every published document each time (unthrottled amplification)
confirmed.evidence:
media_library.sql:94-96:
create policy media_public_read on public.media
  for select to anon
  using (public.media_is_published(id));
store_media.sql:17-24 (final definition):
  select 1 from public.published_documents p
  where jsonb_path_exists(p.data, 'strict $.** ? (@ == $id)', ...)
  or exists (select 1 from public.products pr where pr.status = 'published' and pr.cover_image = p_id::text)
confirmed.failureScenario: The publishable key is baked into the static export, so anyone can send GET <supabase>/rest/v1/media?select=id with no id filter. The RLS predicate is a per-row call to a SECURITY DEFINER function. For every media row, Postgres detoasts and walks every published_documents row (each up to 256 KB) with a recursive .** JSON path, then scans products, which has no index on cover_image. Cost grows as media rows × published JSON size. Repeated anonymous requests, with no throttle in front of PostgREST, burn the shared database CPU up to the anon statement timeout each time. The build's own query filters by id and is unaffected.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Evaluate the published set once per statement. Add public.media_published_ids() returning setof uuid: every UUID-shaped string in published_documents.data (jsonb_path_query with a like_regex on strings) union the published products' cover_image. Recreate the policy as using (id in (select public.media_published_ids())), so Postgres runs it as a single hashed subplan. Grant execute to anon. media_is_published and the rest of the media functions stay as they are.
fixCorrections: The direction is right, but the new function has to keep the old semantics. Add `public.media_published_ids()` returns setof uuid, language sql stable security definer set search_path='': select (s #>> '{}')::uuid from public.published_documents p, jsonb_path_query(p.data, 'strict $.** ? (@.type() == "string" && @ like_regex "^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$")') s union select pr.cover_image::uuid from public.products pr where pr.status='published' and pr.cover_image ~ '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'. The regex must be lowercase-only, because the original `@ == $id` matches only the canonical lowercase text; a case-insensitive match followed by a cast would widen what is public. The products branch needs the same guard, because cover_image is free text up to 120 chars and a bad ::uuid cast would make every anon media read fail. Then revoke from public/anon/authenticated, grant execute to anon, and drop and recreate media_public_read as `using (id in (select public.media_published_ids()))`. Leave media_is_published in place.
reasons: CONFIRM: Confirmed: 20260926090000_media_library.sql:94-96 grants anon select on media with the per-row policy `using (public.media_is_published(id))`, and the final 20260927180000_store_media.sql:10-25 body is a SECURITY DEFINER SQL function (not inlinable), so an unfiltered `GET /rest/v1/media?select=id` with the public key walks every published_documents.data (capped at 256 KB, content_versions_and_publishing.sql:19) with `strict $.**` once per media row. Build/admin callers (src/lib/content.ts:86, journal.ts:46, store.ts) always filter by id, so the fix is harmless to them, and ISSUES.md does not record this vector (its unthrottled-endpoints note at line 45 covers Edge Functions only). Impact is bounded by the anon statement timeout and a small studio's realistic row counts, so it's a low-severity amplification. It is not a correctness or exposure bug.

confirmed.title: A delivery or bounce webhook that arrives before the row's provider_id is stored is never applied to that row

confirmed.failureScenario: email_event_record (lines 433-441) sets `delivery` only for a row whose provider_id is already stored. confirmed.title: publish_version/schedule_version accept a stale seq, so an out-of-date admin tab silently reverts newer live content
confirmed.failureScenario: Saves are conflict-checked (content_versions_next_seq), but publishing is not. PublishBar publishes `seq={baseSeq}`, the latest seq when CollectionForm loaded, and restore always inserts a new seq, so the UI only means to publish the latest version. Step by step: (1) the owner opens post P (latest 5, live 4) and leaves the tab open with no unsaved changes, so canPublish is true. (2) An editor saves seq 6 and publishes it (live 6). (3) The owner clicks «نشر». validateVersion(seq 5) passes and publish_version(seq 5) runs, so live reverts to 5 on the next build. The owner sees «تم بنجاح», and the editor's changes vanish from the public site. schedule_version has the same gap: a stale tab schedules seq 5, which fires later and reverts 6. cancel_schedule in a stale tab removes a newer schedule it never showed. Two simultaneous schedule_version calls for different seqs do not serialize, because the first `update ... where publish_at is not null` cannot see the other's uncommitted row. Both commit, leaving two pending schedules; content_documents shows only the earliest, and when it fires content_go_live silently clears the other.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In a new migration (create or replace), make publish_version, schedule_version and cancel_schedule first take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:' || p_collection::text || ':' || p_doc_id))`, the same key content_versions_next_seq uses. Make publish_version and schedule_version raise errcode 'unique_violation' when p_seq <> (select max(seq) from public.content_versions where collection = p_collection and doc_id = p_doc_id). In src/lib/admin-publish.ts sqlErrorResult, map 23505 to the existing reload/conflict message.
fixCorrections: The SQL part is correct as proposed. Add pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext('content:' || p_collection::text || ':' || p_doc_id)) first in publish_version, schedule_version and cancel_schedule; this is the same key content_versions_next_seq uses, and it also serializes the concurrent double-schedule under READ COMMITTED. Then have publish_version and schedule_version raise when p_seq <> max(seq). On the client, sqlErrorResult cannot reuse an existing code: PublishActionError.code has no conflict member. Add 'CONFLICT' to the union and map 23505 to the reload message, reusing the CONFLICT_MESSAGE text CollectionForm uses for save. cancel_schedule stays only lock-protected: a stale tab can still cancel a schedule it never saw. That is acceptable, or pass the expected scheduled seq if the owner wants it airtight.
reasons: CONFIRM: publish_version/schedule_version (20260927090000_static_site_and_functions.sql:52-95) pass p_seq straight to content_go_live (20260925120000:133-155), which upserts any existing seq with no latest-seq check or lock, and no later migration redefines them. PublishBar is the only caller and always sends seq=baseSeq (CollectionForm.tsx:278), which is only refreshed by load(), so a stale tab with no unsaved edits (canPublish, line 201) republishes an older version and gets a success message. Nothing in ISSUES.md records it. I rate it low, not medium: staff is small, every version is kept, and the audit log records the publish, so the revert is recoverable. It is still a silent revert of live content.

Step 6 then returns QUOTE_CHANGED, which writes nothing except the throttle rows. No order or hold is ever created. The recorded residual risk covers stock held by many emails, not a store-wide lockout from refusals.

The `quote` action (checkout.ts:290, 300/h per IP) gives out a valid quoteHash for free, so the same attacker can make 500 real pending orders on a digital variant (no stock, distinct emails and sessions pass ACTIVE_HOLD) and exhaust the cap anyway. docs/operations.md:359-362 records only the stock-hold residual, not this store-wide lockout. confirmed.title: A product can be saved with a library cover that was deleted while its form was open
confirmed.failureScenario: media_delete sees only saved product covers, and products.cover_image is free text with no existence check. TableForm saves straight to the live row, and unlike content there is no publish check. Step by step: (1) the owner opens a published product's form and picks library image M as the cover without saving yet. (2) An editor deletes M in the media library; media_delete finds no product using M, deletes the row and its objects. (3) The owner clicks حفظ, and the update commits cover_image = M. The next build's resolveCovers cannot find M, and imageSources returns null, so the published product renders with no cover. M is gone from the library, so no «used in» list reveals the dangling id. The media_delete ponytail note relies on 'the publish check', which products do not have.
confirmed.suggestedFix: Add a BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF cover_image trigger on public.products (new migration). When cover_image is uuid-shaped, it runs `perform 1 from public.media where id = new.cover_image::uuid for key share` and raises errcode 'foreign_key_violation' if nothing is found. FOR KEY SHARE conflicts with media_delete's FOR UPDATE, so the two serialize, and either the save or the delete is refused.
fixCorrections: Use the trigger approach, with three details. (1) Make the trigger function SECURITY DEFINER with `set search_path = ''`. It runs as `authenticated`, which is subject to media RLS, and FOR KEY SHARE also needs UPDATE privilege on media. (2) Match the uuid shape with the same rule `isMediaId` uses, so manifest ids pass. Then run `perform 1 from public.media where id = new.cover_image::uuid for key share; if not found then raise ... using errcode = 'foreign_key_violation'`. (3) Fire it on BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE OF cover_image on public.products. Under read committed, whichever side locks second either sees the product (and the delete is refused) or finds no row (and the save is refused). Optionally map 23503 in TableForm to a clear message, for example that the cover image was deleted.
reasons: CONFIRM: media_delete (20260927180000_store_media.sql:66-70) checks only saved product rows, and products.cover_image (20260927160000_catalog_and_checkout.sql:120) is free text with no existence check. TableForm.save (TableForm.tsx:186-193) writes the live row directly, and the original media_delete note (20260926090000_media_library.sql:327-328) relies on a publish check that products do not have. A dangling uuid passes through replaceMediaIds unchanged (content.ts:102); imageSources returns null for a bare media id (images.ts:40); Picture renders nothing (Picture.tsx:33). So the published product silently loses its cover. The race needs two staff sessions and is not recorded in ISSUES.md.

confirmed.title: Four media ticket rejection tests fail for another reason, so they pass even if the guard they name is removed

confirmed.title: The real-PDF ligature check never looks for the reversed «الإ», and its length assertion is always true
confirmed.evidence:
expect(fixed).not.toMatch(/األ|اآل/)
expect(fixed.length).toBe(raw.length)
confirmed.failureScenario: book-preview.ts documents that pdf.js turns «الإهداء» into «اإلهداء». The reference text has «الإ» on pages 1, 2 and 5 (5 occurrences), yet the negative regex checks only the reversed «الأ» and «الآ». If fixLigatures stopped repairing the hamza-below case on the real PDF (for example because the pypdf reference punctuation drifted), the reader would show «اإلهداء» and this test would still pass. `fixed.length === raw.length` holds by construction, because fixLigatures only swaps characters in place.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In tests/unit/reader-mapping.test.ts:171, use /األ|اإل|اآل/ (alef followed by alef-with-hamza never occurs in Arabic) and drop the tautological length assertion.
fixCorrections: Keep the /األ|اآل/ check and drop the tautological length assertion. Add a targeted positive check for the hamza-below case instead of a blanket /اإل/ ban, e.g. `if (n === 1) { expect(raw).toMatch(/اإلهداء/); expect(fixed).toContain('الإهداء'); expect(fixed).not.toContain('اإلهداء') }`, or a lookahead that excludes «إلى», such as /اإل(?!ى)/.
reasons: CONFIRM: tests/unit/reader-mapping.test.ts:171 checks only /األ|اآل/, so a regression in the hamza-below case («اإلهداء», documented at src/lib/book-preview.ts:141) would pass; and line 172 is tautological because fixLigatures only swaps characters in place (book-preview.ts:167-171), so the output length always equals the input length. The suggested blanket /اإل/ ban is unsafe, though: the function doc (book-preview.ts:144-145) says a line break can legitimately run «…ها» into «إلى», and the reference text has «خطواتها إلى» and «وروائحها إلى» on page 2, so a join with no space could fail the test for no real reason.

confirmed.title: tsconfig excludes .next, so Next's route validator (.next/types/validator.ts) is never type-checked by pnpm typecheck, CI or next build
confirmed.evidence:

"exclude": [
    "node_modules",
    "supabase/functions",
    ".next",
confirmed.failureScenario: `exclude` filters the results of `include`, so the explicit `.next/types/**/*.ts` includes do nothing. `tsc -p tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly` lists only `.next/dev/types/routes.d.ts` and `root-params.d.ts`, which come in through next-env.d.ts imports. It never lists `.next/types/validator.ts` or `.next/dev/types/validator.ts`, although both files exist. `next build` checks the same file list (node_modules/next/dist/lib/typescript/runTypeCheck.js:35 uses `effectiveConfiguration.fileNames`), so Next's check of page and layout exports is off everywhere. Example: a layout that requires a slot prop the route does not have, or a page file with a default export that is not a component, passes lint, typecheck, CI and the build, then breaks at render. Today there is no hidden error: I ran a scratch config with `.next` removed from exclude and both validators included, and tsc exited 0.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In tsconfig.json, remove `".next"` from `exclude`. The include globs already limit `.next` to its types folders, and `.next` holds no other .ts files. I verified this with a scratch tsconfig: both validator.ts files are included and tsc exits 0.
fixCorrections: The fix is right: remove ".next" from exclude and change nothing else. One caveat to record: plain `pnpm typecheck` will then also check .next/dev/types/validator.ts, which can go stale after a route is deleted. next build filters those files out, but tsc does not, so a stale dev validator can fail typecheck until the dev server regenerates it or .next/dev is cleared. CI is unaffected because .next does not exist there before typecheck.
reasons: CONFIRM: tsconfig.json:52 excludes ".next", and exclude takes precedence over include (tsconfig.json:44-47). I ran `tsc -p tsconfig.json --listFilesOnly`: the only .next files it lists are .next/dev/types/routes.d.ts and root-params.d.ts, which arrive through the next-env.d.ts imports, even though .next/types/validator.ts and .next/dev/types/validator.ts both exist. next build reads the same effectiveConfiguration.fileNames (runTypeCheck.js), so the route export validator never runs in typecheck, CI (ci.yml:53) or the build. That makes it a real, reachable config gap, but no defect is live today.

confirmed.title: Dead export `boundedText` in http.ts while three handlers inline the same body-limit logic
confirmed.failureScenario: No runtime bug: the helper is never called, so the shared JSON contract module ships an unused function and the same 8-line limit check is maintained in three places (a limit fix in one handler silently misses the others).
confirmed.suggestedFix: Either delete `boundedText` from supabase/functions/_shared/http.ts, or (smaller total diff) use it in checkout.ts/contact.ts (`const text = await boundedText(request, MAX_BODY_BYTES); if (text === null) return fail(413, ...)`) and drop checkout.ts's duplicate MAX_DECLARED_BODY_BYTES. contact.ts keeps its larger declared limit only if that difference is intended.
fixCorrections: Do not delete boundedText. Fix it as described under S07.2 and use it in the three handlers; that removes both the dead code and the duplicated logic. contact.ts's 32 KiB declared limit (contact.ts:34) serves no purpose once the read is streamed and bounded at 8 KiB, so drop it rather than preserve it.
reasons: CONFIRM: grep finds boundedText only at its definition (http.ts:37). contact.ts:124-133, checkout.ts:244-252 and resend-webhook.ts:113-128 each hand-roll the same check. checkout.ts:28 and :30 define two constants with the same value, 65_536. This duplicates S07.2 and has no runtime impact of its own, so the S07.2 fix closes it.

confirmed.title: Import maps list `image-size` for functions that never load media.ts
confirmed.evidence:
"image-size": "npm:image-size@2.0.4",
-- import graph: contact → contact.ts → db, env, http, rate-limit, turnstile; resend-webhook → resend-webhook.ts → db, email, env. Neither reaches media.ts, the only `image-size` importer. Needed only in admin/ and outbox/ (jobs.ts → admin.ts → media.ts).

Deno resolves npm specifiers only when they are imported, so there is no bundle or runtime effect, which makes this cleanup (info) rather than a low-severity defect.

confirmed.title: motion.spec skips a story page that returns 404 instead of failing
confirmed.evidence:
const missing = response?.status() === 404 || (await page.locator('main h1').first().textContent())?.includes('هذا الطريق')
test.skip(Boolean(missing), `${path} is not in this build (the local seed's demo product)`)
confirmed.failureScenario: The skip is meant only for /store/demo-khous, but it applies to every STORY route. The header comment says this spec also runs against the static export (PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=http://localhost:4010). If that export drops /book, /scenes or /contact (it answers the woven 404, whose h1 is «هذا الطريق لم يُبنَ بعد»), the test is reported as skipped, not failed, and the missing page ships unnoticed.
confirmed.suggestedFix: In motion.spec.ts, limit the skip to the seed-only route: `test.skip(path === '/store/demo-khous' && Boolean(missing), ...)`. Every other route should fail on 404.
reasons: CONFIRM: Code truth holds: tests/e2e/motion.spec.ts:108-109 applies the 404/«هذا الطريق» skip to every STORY route, though the comment at :107 says it is only meant for the seed-only /store/demo-khous. The claimed impact does not hold, though: tests/e2e/public.spec.ts:10,26-27 checks every other STORY route ('/', '/book', '/scenes', '/contact', ...) with `expect(response?.ok()).toBeTruthy()`, so a missing page still fails the suite. What remains is only a lost motion signal in this one spec. Low-value tidy-up; the suggested fix is right.

rejected.title: `canonicalJson` copied verbatim between the browser cart and the checkout function
reasons: REFUTE: The browser fingerprint (cart.ts:208-210) is only compared with the browser's own earlier fingerprint to decide whether to reuse the idempotency key. It is never compared with the server's requestHash (checkout.ts:354), so the two canonicalJson copies can differ without any effect. What matters for parity is normalizedCore, not canonicalJson. The duplication is a style point with no reachable defect.

rejected.title: The empty scenes gallery shows a 50vh blank weave block before its «لا توجد مَشاهد بعد» message
reasons: REFUTE: Code matches the claim: with items=[], SceneGallery.tsx:63-131 still renders the title band, a lone «الكل» toggle, and an empty `<ul aria-label="الصور">` that is 50vh tall with the weave background (scenes.module.css:37-39). page.tsx:19-23 then adds the message below it. rejected.title: visual.spec passes on and captures error or 404 pages as design evidence
